name: Fisticuffs (Mac Robinson & Brian Warfield)
sources: style-research-extended-2 vol.2 trap-soul — Fisticuffs (Mac Robinson & Brian Warfield)
notes: The board behind the lane's most atmospheric female catalogue. "The most static harmony in this section — a single m9/m11 sonority, or an `i–VI` pair, held for a whole track, with a chord **inversion** rather than a chord change used as the lift", so the one-chord family sits at top weight and `harmonicRhythm` is nearly all `vamp`; the entry names A minor, D♭ minor and F♯ minor as the recurring centres. ⚠ **This duo and the Jhené Aiko artist model describe the same records by design, and the roster allows that overlap.** What is authored differently is what the two entries themselves say differently: this one adds "live-feel kit and hand percussion on the band-tracked material" and requires **both** low ends — "a sustained low sine with slow portamento and an extremely long decay on the electronic cuts, and a **played electric bass with real motion** on the band cuts. Both variants are required" — so the perc block here is real rather than empty and the 808 keeps a working slide rate, where hers is almost inert. The rest of the kit is the shared description: "a soft 808 kick on 1 and the 16th before 3, a clap or snap on beat 3 with a very long reverb tail, hats sparse (often a single 16th pair per bar) and **no rolls**, plus whole verses with no percussion." The palette sentence is the section's most-copied and is recorded here because it drives the melody's timbre and register: "nylon and clean electric guitar arpeggios, harp and bell textures, filtered Rhodes, and field-recording ambience". ⚠ The **INFERRED** parameters are the swing amount, every drum number and the 808 figures; the entry marks drum values as folded/inferred. ⚠ `confidence` is medium, mirroring the entry. ⚠ `session.bpm.mode` is **INFERRED**: the number is not stated in the entry, and it is an authored centre of gravity inside the band the entry does state. ⚠ **The last two values in `session.keys` are INFERRED.** The entry names three — "A minor keys (A minor, D♭ minor, F♯ minor) dominate" — and E minor and B minor are added from the parent lane's own palette, not from the research. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` gained `syncopated_cell` (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry says "**the most static harmony in this section** - a single m9/m11 sonority, or an `i-VI` pair, held for a whole track, with a chord *inversion* rather than a chord change used as the lift". `chordDurationBeats` is the only parameter carrying a loop length, and it was **dead here**: `generators::chords::layout` reads it under `syncopated_cell` alone, which this model did not author — so every generation was one 4-bar hold instead of the documented loop. The sonority itself does not move: over a single-chord family every cell is the same chord re-voiced. ⚠ `chordDurationBeats` narrowed from [8, 32] to [8, 16], and that narrowing is **INFERRED**: the engine can only re-voice at a cell boundary, so a 32-beat cell is eight bars and the documented inversion-lift never landed inside a four-bar clip. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 899/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.26 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. ⚠ The value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "nylon and clean electric guitar arpeggios, harp and bell textures, filtered Rhodes, and field-recording ambience (water, wind) — this palette is their signature and it is what the lane copies. Long pad drones underneath everything.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
